citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The exhibitor is not using appropriate methods to prevent, control, or diagnose and treat diseases as indicated in the
written program of veterinary care (PVC) for treating ectoparasites in capybara when the Attending Veterinarian (AV) is on
holiday. The PVC states to test and treat ectoparasites (such as flies) as needed and to contact a specifically identified
veterinary clinic for emergency/weekend/holiday care. Currently, there are no fly control measures taken other than fly
tape in the food prep kitchen located approximately 30 feet from the capybara enclosures. An adult female capybara ("Tic
Tac") has excessive fly activity around her eyes, which appear reddened and watery. She is observed occasionally
rubbing her eyes with her front foot. Her condition has worsened since last week whereas she now has a moderate
amount of white discharge and crusts around her left eye. During the 06 October 2026 licensing inspection, the applicant
stated she had ordered an eye medication through the AV for Tic Tac's eye condition. The inspector called the AV's clinic
and the receptionist indicated the AV was out of country for 2 weeks. When this was discussed with the applicant, she
stated she would have another veterinarian prescribe medication. As of today's inspection, the animal has not received
treatment, nor has the emergency/weekend/holiday care veterinary clinic been contacted to address Tic Tac's condition.
The applicant stated the AV is next available to assess the capybara in 5 days. Failure to follow the written PVC for
animal care and treatment can result in discomfort of the animal and prolonged duration of disease or other complications.
Correct by contacting the emergency/weekend/holiday veterinary clinic identified in the PVC to alert a veterinarian of Tic
Tac's eye condition by 15 October 2026.
This is a 2nd Re-License Inspection for a Class “C” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 1 more inspection or by 05 December 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
You may appeal this finding in writing by 21 October 2026.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
